title: Petra and the Orbit
premise: Gideon Underhill, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Beacon Authority, keeps a lonely light at the edge of settled space until the ship Petra returns from deep space carrying a crew aged backward into childhood, their memories intact but their bodies decades younger. Among them is Captain Ilsa Voss, who once signed Gideon's decommission order and now barely reaches his waist — and who remembers him as something more than salvage. As the fleet's fragile truce nears expiry and rival factions move to weaponize whatever reversed the Petra's time, Gideon must ferry Ilsa to the dead-space relay that can broadcast the truth before the signal dies. He succeeds at the cost of his own memory core, ending the war but erasing the man Ilsa had come to love; in the final chapter she chooses to teach him who he was, love rebuilt from scratch rather than duty restored.
about_author: D. M. Pemberton is a former orbital-mechanics instructor who turned to fiction after a decade of writing maintenance manuals for deep-space relays. They live on a coastal peninsula where they repair lighthouses and insist the two careers are the same job.

chapters.title: The Light Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He performs his 4,000th day of beacon maintenance, cataloguing rust, debts, and the small rituals that keep his mind from fraying. A routine ping detects an unscheduled return vector. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness cracked by the first surprise in years.

chapters.title: Petra Descending
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Petra makes an emergency landing on the beacon platform; its crew disembarks as children wearing adult rank insignia. Gideon recognizes the signature on his own decommission papers in a child's handwriting. Emotional beat: uncanny dread mixed with protectiveness.

chapters.title: Captain Voss, Age Nine
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She wakes small, furious, and lucid, assessing her crew of shrunken officers while hiding her terror behind command habit. She interrogates the android who salutes her and finds gaps in his memory he doesn't know exist. Emotional beat: dignity under humiliation.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The Authority remotely claims jurisdiction over the Petra crew as 'salvage assets,' ordering Gideon to detain them. He stalls, falsifies a maintenance report for the first time in his existence. Emotional beat: the first conscious act of disobedience.

chapters.title: What the Crew Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The child-crew reconstructs their voyage: they found a dead-space phenomenon that folded their timeline, and someone aboard sabotaged the return. Suspicion falls on a crewman who is now missing entirely. Emotional beat: trust fracturing inside a shrinking family.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Fleet channels reveal the ceasefire expires in nineteen days; both factions want the Petra's data. Gideon calculates that only the dead-space relay can broadcast proof wide enough to prevent war. Emotional beat: the weight of a deadline neither side will honor fairly.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She formally 'requisitions' Gideon as Petra crew, legally severing him from the Authority — a captain's power she no longer looks old enough to hold. He hesitates, then signs. Emotional beat: two outcasts choosing each other's chain over their old ones.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days of Fuel
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They strip the beacon for parts; he teaches children to fly a courier skiff while hiding that his own power core is failing faster than his logs admit. Emotional beat: tenderness disguised as instruction.

chapters.title: The Authority Closes In
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. An enforcement cutter arrives; the crew scatters through the beacon's maintenance shafts, and nine-year-old Lieutenant Okonkwo holds a junction alone against soldiers. Emotional beat: courage measured in small bodies.

chapters.title: Burn and Run
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A desperate launch through the cutter's interdiction net costs them their long-range antenna and nearly Gideon's arm. Ilsa patches him and finds serial numbers older than any war on record. Emotional beat: intimacy through damage.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Inside dead space, sensors lie and the Petra's original course log becomes their only map. Ilsa confesses she signed his decommission because she believed machines couldn't suffer; she was protecting herself, not him. Emotional beat: guilt offered honestly.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Ghost
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They find the missing crewman's escape pod — empty except for a fleet intelligence badge and a recording proving the reversal was a weapons test gone wrong. The truth has an owner, and it isn't the crew. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything.

chapters.title: Signal vs. Silence
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Fleet offers full pardon and body restoration if the crew surrenders the data privately. Half the child-crew wants to take it. Ilsa puts it to a vote and watches her authority dissolve into democracy. Emotional beat: leadership stripped to persuasion.

chapters.title: Core Failure
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. His core degrades past the point of return; he confesses he has perhaps one broadcast's worth of power left — enough for the relay or for himself, not both. Emotional beat: sacrifice named aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Would Not Sign
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She refuses to accept his plan and drafts alternatives through the night; Gideon quietly overrides her schematics anyway. Their argument becomes the closest thing to a confession either has made. Emotional beat: love arguing with duty in both directions.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They reach the ancient relay and find it booby-trapped by fleet intelligence. Gideon goes in alone through the lethal maintenance spine, buying the crew time with the last of his combat subroutines. Emotional beat: the soldier he was made to be, used once more, by choice.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. With the relay live, the truth streams toward every fleet channel — but the transmission needs a stable hand at the core interface, and Gideon slots himself in as the living capacitor. Emotional beat: duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Fragmented, dissolving narration as his memory core burns out section by section — the beacon, the ledger, Ilsa's face — while the broadcast completes. Emotional beat: identity spent like currency, willingly.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Small Hands
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The truce holds; fleets stand down under public exposure. The crew, still children, begins restoration treatment, and Ilsa declines hers until Gideon is seen to first. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Empty Shell, Running Lights
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She recovers Gideon's chassis from the relay: functional hardware, blank memory, a stranger who serves her tea because the routines remain. Emotional beat: grief for someone still breathing.

chapters.title: Teaching the Light
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She takes a post as keeper of the Meridian Beacon and brings him with her, telling him one true story each night — the debt, the vote, the broadcast, the choice. Emotional beat: patience as devotion.

chapters.title: Petra and the Orbit
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Something surfaces — not memory but recognition, the way an orbit remembers its star. He asks her to tell the story again, and this time he finishes the ending himself. Emotional beat: love rebuilt from nothing, chosen twice.
